We need to read problem statement carefully: The problem description appears to be confusing: The title says: "Your laptop keyboard is faulty, and whenever you type a character 'i' on it, it doesn't reverse the string that you have written." The description says: "Return the final string that will be present on your laptop screen, but this time, make sure that the string remains unchanged even when you type an 'i'.

Actually reading the examples: Example 1 s="string". Input: s = "string". Output: "string". Explanation says that after typing first character, text is "s". After second, "st". After third, "str". Since fourth char is 'i', the text doesn't change and remains "str". After fifth char, text is "strin". After sixth char, text is "string". So they say that when you type i, you do NOT reverse, i.e., you do nothing (the text remains unchanged). So the keyboard is faulty such that when you type an 'i', the string doesn't get reversed (maybe the intention of the original problem: the keyboard incorrectly reverses the string each time you type 'i', but here they ask to "make sure that the string remains unchanged even when you type an 'i'". Wait there's confusion. Actually I think the original problem (like Leetcode problem 2810 "Faulty Keyboard") is that whenever you type an 'i', it reverses the string typed so far. For other characters, they are appended at the end. The problem asks you to simulate the process and return the final string. For example, given s = "string", we have: type 's': "s". type 't': "st". type 'r': "str". type 'i': reverse => "rts". type 'n': "rtsn". type 'g': "rtsng". So output should be "rtsng". Actually known LeetCode 2810: Input: s = "string" Output: "rtsng". Explanation: "s"-> "s", "t"-> "st", "r"-> "str", "i"-> reverse => "rts", "n"-> "rtsn", "g"-> "rtsng". So why this problem statement says "when you type i, it doesn't reverse the string"??? That seems contradictory.
